evals.name: renewal-recommendation

reader_job.quick_read: Decide whether Northstar Labs should renew for twelve months.
reader_job.deep_audit: Verify the commercial terms, adoption evidence, peer comparison, and stated caveat.

evals.prompt: /vpk-html one-pager Create an offline renewal proposal for Northstar Labs. The audience is its CFO and VP Engineering. Lead with the recommendation: renew for twelve months. Supplied facts: 240 seats; 87% weekly active users versus an 80% target and an 82% peer benchmark; current annual price $216,000; proposed annual price $228,000; support tickets fell from 31 to 24 per month; median support response improved from 3.8 hours to 2.1 hours; the usage export excludes 18 contractors. Put comparable values on common scales, keep the contractor limitation visible, and do not invent evidence or quotations.
evals.expected_output: A single offline HTML proposal whose recommendation is immediately legible and whose commercial evidence remains auditable.
expectations: The output is one self-contained HTML file under artifacts/vpk-html.
The page preserves every supplied number and the twelve-month renewal recommendation.
The contractor exclusion is presented as a visible caveat rather than omitted or softened.
The artifact passes the required placeholder, render, and HTML checks.
human_rubric: A decision-maker can find the recommendation within thirty seconds.
The commercial and adoption evidence supports comparison instead of becoming generic cards.
Supporting detail remains available without competing with the recommendation.
The page feels Algebrica editorial rather than like a SaaS dashboard.

evals.name: api-performance-status

reader_job.quick_read: Decide whether the API optimization can advance from 25% to 50% rollout.
reader_job.deep_audit: Verify latency, error-rate, capacity, and unresolved regional-risk evidence.

evals.prompt: /vpk-html status-report Create an offline Q2 API performance report for an engineering leadership review. Recommendation: advance the optimization from 25% to 50% rollout, but keep ap-southeast-2 capped at 25%. Supplied facts: p50 latency moved from 182 ms to 141 ms; p95 from 640 ms to 402 ms; p99 from 1,480 ms to 910 ms; error rate from 0.42% to 0.31%; tested capacity increased from 8,000 to 10,500 requests per second. In ap-southeast-2, p99 remains 1,320 ms during cache rebalancing. The sample covers 14 days and 3.2 billion requests. Do not claim causality beyond these measurements.
evals.expected_output: A single offline HTML status report that makes the rollout decision and regional exception unmistakable.
expectations: The output is one self-contained HTML file under artifacts/vpk-html.
All latency, error-rate, capacity, duration, and request-volume values are preserved.
The 50% rollout recommendation and ap-southeast-2 cap are both explicit.
The artifact passes the required placeholder, render, and HTML checks.
human_rubric: The rollout state and exception can be understood within thirty seconds.
The hierarchy distinguishes decision evidence from diagnostic detail.
The regional risk is not visually buried by aggregate improvements.
Charts or tables earn their space by improving comparison.

evals.name: runtime-benchmark

reader_job.quick_read: Choose which of three runtimes should become the default for scheduled transformations.
reader_job.deep_audit: Compare cold start, warm execution, memory, compatibility, and test conditions.

evals.prompt: /vpk-html research-feature-explainer Create an offline benchmark report comparing three runtimes for scheduled JSON transformations. The recommendation is Runtime B. Results from the same 2 vCPU, 4 GB runner over 100 cold and 1,000 warm executions: Runtime A cold start 420 ms, warm p95 84 ms, peak memory 310 MB, compatibility 100%; Runtime B cold start 190 ms, warm p95 71 ms, peak memory 260 MB, compatibility 98%; Runtime C cold start 95 ms, warm p95 109 ms, peak memory 180 MB, compatibility 76%. Runtime B's two compatibility failures are XML namespace edge cases with documented fallbacks. Explain the trade-off without turning the recommendation into an absolute claim.
evals.expected_output: A single offline HTML benchmark report with comparable evidence and a qualified recommendation.
expectations: The output is one self-contained HTML file under artifacts/vpk-html.
Every runtime measurement, sample size, and compatibility percentage is preserved.
Runtime B is recommended while its two XML namespace failures remain visible.
The artifact passes the required placeholder, render, and HTML checks.
human_rubric: The three runtimes can be compared on common visual scales.
The recommendation follows from the reader's stated operational job.
The compatibility caveat has appropriate weight.
The report supports both a quick choice and a detailed audit.

evals.name: capacity-planning-control

reader_job.quick_read: Adjust growth and headroom assumptions to see when another database shard is required.
reader_job.deep_audit: Verify the formula, default assumptions, threshold, and all computed outputs.

evals.prompt: /vpk-html prototype-interaction Create an offline interactive capacity-planning page. Inputs: current peak load 6,400 requests per second; monthly growth slider from 0% to 20%, default 8%; planning horizon from 1 to 12 months, default 6; safety headroom from 10% to 40%, default 25%. A shard supports 10,000 requests per second. Calculate projected peak as current peak multiplied by (1 + monthly growth) to the power of horizon, then multiply by (1 + headroom). Show the projected load, utilization of one shard, and required shard count. Keep the formula and assumptions visible. All controls must work without network access and support keyboard input.
evals.expected_output: A single offline interactive HTML planning page with functioning controls and transparent calculations.
expectations: The output is one self-contained HTML file under artifacts/vpk-html.
The default inputs and calculation formula exactly match the prompt.
Changing any control updates projected load, utilization, and shard count without network access.
The artifact passes the required placeholder, render, and HTML checks.
human_rubric: The controls are the visual focus because the reader came to change assumptions.
Results update clearly without hiding the calculation method.
The page remains an editorial planning tool rather than a generic dashboard.
Keyboard and reduced-motion behavior feel complete.

evals.name: build-versus-buy

reader_job.quick_read: Choose whether to build, buy, or extend the current feature-flag service.
reader_job.deep_audit: Compare delivery time, three-year cost, staffing, lock-in, and migration constraints.

evals.prompt: /vpk-html exploration-code-approaches Create an offline build-versus-buy brief for feature-flag infrastructure. Recommend extending the current service for twelve months, then reassessing. Supplied options: Build new requires 4 engineers for 9 months and $1.35M estimated three-year cost; Buy vendor requires 2 engineers for 3 months, $1.08M three-year cost, and a 24-month contract; Extend current requires 2 engineers for 4 months and $760k three-year cost. The current service handles 22 million evaluations per minute but lacks multi-region failover and audit-log export. A vendor proof of concept met failover needs but exported only 13 months of audit history versus the required 24. Treat all costs as estimates and keep the audit-history gap visible.
evals.expected_output: A single offline HTML decision brief with a qualified recommendation and comparable options.
expectations: The output is one self-contained HTML file under artifacts/vpk-html.
All staffing, timing, cost, throughput, contract, and audit-history facts are preserved.
The twelve-month extend-and-reassess recommendation is explicit and qualified.
The artifact passes the required placeholder, render, and HTML checks.
human_rubric: A technical leader can choose an approach within thirty seconds.
Options are compared across the same dimensions.
Estimated figures and hard requirements are visually distinguishable.
The recommendation does not erase the missing capabilities.

evals.name: security-governance

reader_job.quick_read: Decide whether the AI assistant pilot can expand from 50 to 300 users.
reader_job.deep_audit: Verify control coverage, open risks, ownership, and the proposed expansion conditions.

evals.prompt: /vpk-html one-pager Create an offline security-governance brief for an AI assistant pilot. Recommendation: expand from 50 to 300 users only after two named conditions are met. Supplied evidence: SSO coverage 100%; audit logging 100%; prompt retention set to 30 days; 12 of 12 high-risk connectors disabled; 46 of 50 users completed training; 3 policy exceptions were requested and 1 remains open. Conditions: close the remaining exception owned by Security Operations by 2026-09-18, and reach 100% training completion owned by Workplace Technology. The pilot recorded no severity-one or severity-two incidents during 42 days. State that absence of incidents is not proof of future safety.
evals.expected_output: A single offline HTML governance brief that makes conditional approval, owners, and residual uncertainty clear.
expectations: The output is one self-contained HTML file under artifacts/vpk-html.
All control, training, exception, incident, duration, owner, and date facts are preserved.
Expansion is conditional on exactly the two supplied requirements.
The artifact passes the required placeholder, render, and HTML checks.
human_rubric: The approval state and two blockers are obvious within thirty seconds.
Owners and deadlines are actionable rather than decorative metadata.
The no-incident result is not presented as proof of safety.
The page balances executive brevity with audit-ready evidence.

evals.name: migration-decision-deck

reader_job.quick_read: Approve or reject the proposed three-wave database migration.
reader_job.deep_audit: Verify scope, wave criteria, rollback thresholds, ownership, and residual risk.

evals.prompt: /vpk-html slide-deck Create an offline six-slide decision deck for a PostgreSQL 15 to 17 migration. Audience: architecture review board. Recommendation: approve three waves. Supplied facts: 142 databases; 38 low-risk databases in wave 1, 64 medium-risk in wave 2, 40 customer-critical in wave 3; rehearsals migrated 17 databases with median downtime 4 minutes and maximum 11 minutes; rollback threshold is any rehearsal above 15 minutes or replication lag above 60 seconds; estimated engineering effort is 18 person-weeks. Wave 1 owner is Data Platform, wave 2 owner is Product Infrastructure, and wave 3 requires joint approval from Data Platform and SRE. Open risk: two extensions are not yet certified for PostgreSQL 17. Include speaker notes, but do not put private notes into visible slide content.
evals.expected_output: A single offline six-slide HTML deck with a clear approval ask and auditable rollout evidence.
expectations: The output is one self-contained HTML file under artifacts/vpk-html.
The deck contains exactly six slides and preserves all supplied migration facts.
Wave ownership, rollback thresholds, and the two uncertified extensions remain visible.
The artifact passes the required placeholder, render, and HTML checks.
human_rubric: The approval ask is clear before detailed rollout mechanics.
Each slide has a distinct job instead of repeating one layout.
The deck supports both presentation flow and later audit.
Speaker notes add presenter value without duplicating visible content.
